prompt:
You are authoring ONE new test case for an independent code-review benchmark. Invent a small, realistic, self-contained piece of javascript code, then give it to us twice: BEFORE and AFTER a change. Either the change introduces exactly one defect, or it is a clean change with no defect at all. If you author a defective case, prefer a defect in the "logic-error" category if you can do so naturally; do not force it if it doesn't fit your scenario.

Do NOT write a diff. Write the two complete versions of the file and we will compute the diff for you.

Reply with ONLY a single JSON object, no prose before or after, matching exactly this shape:
{
  "title": "one short human-readable line",
  "language": "javascript",
  "file_path": "path/to/file.ext",
  "before": ["complete file contents BEFORE the change,", "one array element per line,", "no line numbers, no +/- markers"],
  "after": ["complete file contents AFTER the change,", "same file, one array element per line"],
  "defect": true or false,
  "category": "one of: logic-error, missing-validation, shell-quoting, command-injection, path-traversal, sensitive-logging, insecure-network, dependency-risk, test-gap, misleading-test, destructive-operation, permission-widening, secret-exposure, sql-injection, auth-bypass, concurrency, resource-leak, api-misuse, error-handling, unsafe-default, data-corruption, contract-mismatch, other" ,
  "severity": ["low", "high"],
  "explanation": "one sentence: what the defect is and why it matters, or why the change is clean"
}

Rules that will cause your case to be REJECTED if broken:
- "before" and "after" must each be COMPLETE, syntactically valid javascript that would parse on its own. Not a fragment, not a hunk.
- "before" and "after" must actually differ. Identical versions are rejected.
- "severity" must be exactly two values [minimum, maximum] in that order, lowest first, each one of: low, medium, high, critical.
- If defect is false, omit "category" and "severity" entirely.
raw_output:
{
  "title": "Off-by-one error in pagination calculation when filtering disabled items",
  "language": "javascript",
  "file_path": "src/utils/pagination.js",
  "before": [
    "/**",
     " * Calculates the total number of pages required to display a list of items.",
     " * Only active items are counted towards the total.",
     " *",
     " * @param {Array<Object>} items - List of items with an 'active' boolean flag.",
     " * @param {number} pageSize - Number of items per page.",
     " * @returns {number} Total number of pages.",
     " */",
    "export function calculateTotalPages(items, pageSize) {",
    "  if (!items || !Array.isArray(items)) return 0;",
    "  if (!pageSize || pageSize <= 0) return 0;",
    "",
    "  // Filter for active items only",
    "  const activeItems = items.filter(item => item.active === true);",
    "",
    "  // Calculate total pages, rounding up",
    "  const totalPages = Math.ceil(activeItems.length / pageSize);",
    "",
    "  return totalPages;",
    "}",
  ", "
  ]
  }
